Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. As we continue the FinBank SIG intake, the assessor team has a few follow-ups specific to your build/CI controls so we can map them to SIG and SOC2 control objectives. High-level asks:

- A short inventory of CI jobs that perform production builds + their owners (we need owner and last-modified).
- Evidence of code review enforcement (sample PR with review history is fine, redacted if necessary).
- Artifact signing or provenance statements (how do you assert the artifact minted in CI is what was deployed?).
- Secrets handling: how are credentials injected into CI? rotation cadence?
- Change approvals: brief summary of your change approval gates for production deploys.

Can you get these items into a single package or point me to a shared folder this week? Ideally by EOD Friday (2028-03-17) so the assessor can schedule their mapping session.

If there are any sensitivity constraints, flag them and we can agree on redaction rules.

Thanks — Alex

Alex / Marissa — attaching the sanitized job export and a short description of what each job does. Notes:

- Export includes only production build jobs (tagged prod-build) and owner metadata. We stripped job-level secrets and replaced values with placeholders.
- CI platform: internally called "ForgeCI" (Jenkins core + orchestration). Production build jobs create a signed artifact by calling our provenance service that attaches a UUID + signature header to the artifact manifest. The private key is held in KMS (AWS KMS in prod region).
- Secret injection: we use short-lived tokens minted by our credential broker (ephemeral vault leases, rotated every 1 hour). Tokens are never persisted in job definitions.

Small excerpt from deploy audit (redacted):
> 2028-03-10T23:14:05Z - job=prod-build-webapp - artifact=sha256:... - signer=provenance-service - deployer=jdoe_redacted - deploy_stage=canary

I attached:
- jenkins-job-export.yaml (sanitized job definitions)
- deploy-audit-sample.log (redacted deploy audit lines)

If the assessor needs a KMS policy snapshot or the provenance service code snippet, we can provide a scoped export under IRM approval.

Alex, Marissa — adding a short note on artifact provenance and change approval flow:

- Artifact provenance: every CI build emits a signed manifest including build inputs (git commit SHA, build image, table of dependency checksums). The manifest is signed by the provenance-service key. At deploy time the orchestrator verifies the manifest signature before promoting.
- Release gating: production promotion requires: 2 approving reviews on PRs touching prod paths, successful integration + static analysis + SBOM generation, and an explicit "promote" action from the release manager. The promote action creates a signed change ticket in our change ledger (immutable audit stream).
- Secrets: credential broker leases ephemeral access tokens from Vault (1hr TTL); we enforce vault-role scoped access. Rotation cadence for long-lived KMS keys is 2 years; we use envelope keys rotated every 90 days.

I also attached a short sanitized PR export (code-review-sample.patch) showing approval timestamps.

If GlobalSecure wants timelines mapped to specific SIG control IDs, Irene is the right person to map — but I can annotate the technical evidence for each control.

-Karthik

Alex — thanks for the checklist. I've mapped the submitted artifacts to the relevant SIG categories and added recommendations for redaction and scope:

1) Code review (SIG: PR.1 / PR.2): code-review-sample.patch -> includes reviewer IDs and timestamps. Recommend redacting user email addresses and exporting only the review log with approval stamps.
2) CI inventory (SIG: CI.1): jenkins-job-export.yaml and ci-access-matrix.csv -> keep owner usernames but redact SSH fingerprints.
3) Artifact provenance (SIG: AR.1): provenance manifests + deploy-audit-sample.log -> include manifest signatures and verification steps; redact exact artifact hashes if required.
4) Secrets management (SIG: SM.3): high-level description is fine for intake; for deeper testing we'll provide scoped Vault role exports under an IRM-approved request.
5) Change control (SIG: CH.2): change ledger entries are immutable; we can export a time-windowed view with ticket IDs and approval timestamps.
